clue.text: Library could be almost noble idea

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters may be rearranged into something else entirely
almost means the word noble stops short of its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a library might be an almost noble idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims noble to NOBL; with IDEA these letters are what 'could be' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bodleian is the main research library of Oxford University.

clue.text: One of the Archers at the sharp end?

definitions.text: One of the Archers at the sharp end?

parts.words: One of the Archers at the sharp end?
parts.note: an archer is literally a fighter with a bow, while the rower nearest the pointed front of a boat bears the same name; The Archers is also a long-running BBC radio soap

explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a long-running BBC radio soap, a red herring; the answer is both a fighter with a bow and the oarsman at a boat's bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier with a longbow, and also the rower seated nearest a boat's pointed front.

clue.text: When following the scent this animal won't be foxed

definitions.text: When following the scent this animal won't be foxed

parts.words: When following the scent this animal won't be foxed
parts.note: a dog trained to follow an artificial trail laid instead of a live quarry, so it never chases a fox

explanation.walkthrough: 'foxed' means puzzled, but also hints the hunt has no fox: this hound follows a dragged lure.
explanation.definitionFit: A hound used in a drag hunt, which pursues a trail of laid scent rather than a fox.

clue.text: Being out of humour, you might say, he's bound to dig something up

definitions.text: he's bound to dig something up

indicators.note: you might say points to the spoken form of the preceding phrase

parts.note: ex means out of or formerly, so being out of humour is being ex-humour

explanation.surface: A grumpy person is certain to unearth something.
explanation.walkthrough: EX plus HUMOUR, said aloud, is the word for one who digs up the buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who removes a buried body from the ground is one who digs it up.

clue.text: Pungent corrosive substance swamping river

indicators.note: swamping means flooding over, so the substance surrounds the river

parts.note: an acid is a corrosive chemical

explanation.surface: A sharp-smelling caustic chemical floods a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrid describes a sharp, bitter smell or taste.

clue.text: Improvement in university performance

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at a university, as in 'up at Oxford'
a turn is a short act or performance on stage

explanation.surface: A student's performance at university has got better.
explanation.walkthrough: UP is the British idiom for being at university, so 'in university' supplies it.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn is a rise or turn for the better in fortunes.

clue.text: Describe the harbour bar

parts.note: a port is a harbour for ships
a bar of light is a ray

explanation.surface: A request to give an account of the dockside pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub or sandbank at the harbour mouth; here it is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray someone is to depict them in words or pictures.

clue.text: Get together to knit

definitions.meaning: to join or combine with others
to knit is to join closely, as broken bones knit

explanation.definitionFit: Joining forces, and fusing closely as healing bones do.

clue.text: Late refreshment for a dark international

parts.note: the dark is the night time
a cap is awarded to a player chosen for a national team, so an international is a cap

explanation.surface: A drink is served to a sinister foreign player.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport a player chosen for their country wins a cap, so a cap means an international player.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap is a drink taken just before going to bed.

clue.text: Land held by the church at Rimmon's order

indicators.note: order means the letters are set out in a new arrangement

parts.note: Rimmon is a Syrian god named in the Bible; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A church estate is held at the command of a pagan deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges AT and RIMMON together.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortmain is the inalienable possession of property by a corporation such as a church, literally 'dead hand'.

clue.text: Cladding for a rainy day?

parts.note: read literally, this is the wooden facing that keeps the weather off a house, punning on saving for a rainy day

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'for a rainy day' suggests savings, but the clue is about overlapping boards that shed rain from a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlapping horizontal planks fixed to an outside wall form a weatherproof cladding.

clue.text: A bogus journalist overcome with remorse

parts.note: a sham is something bogus or fake
ED is short for editor, the journalist in charge

explanation.surface: A fraudulent reporter is consumed by guilt.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling shame or guilt for what one has done is the same as being contrite.

clue.text: Wild flower opening on a peak

indicators.note: on in this across clue places the opening after the peak it sits upon

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, as on Dartmoor
a rent is a tear or opening

explanation.surface: A wild flower blooms in a gap on a mountain top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is a thing that flows, not a bloom: a wild flower is a rushing stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A rushing, violent stream of water is something that flows wildly.

clue.text: Regular Army finds him a trouble-maker

definitions.text: Regular Army finds him a trouble-maker

parts.words: Regular Army finds him a trouble-maker
parts.note: the regular forces of a country are harried by an irregular fighter waging hit-and-run war

explanation.walkthrough: 'Regular' looks like an anagram signal, but the clue simply describes the soldiers' irregular opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a small independent band fighting regular troops by ambush and sabotage.

clue.text: Delayed about a minute to collect the plates together

indicators.note: about means the delayed word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: Someone running late takes a minute to gather up the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plates' suggests crockery; here they are thin layers.
explanation.definitionFit: To laminate is to bond thin layers into one sheet.

clue.text: It may get you to a university after you initially make a bloomer

indicators.note: after puts the admissions body behind the initial letter
initially takes just the opening letter of the word you

parts.words: It may get you to a university
parts.note: UCCA was the Universities Central Council on Admissions, the old British body handling university applications

explanation.surface: Something may help you into university after you initially blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a bloomer' suggests a blunder, but a bloomer here is something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a flowering plant of the agave family, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Walk out with Denry or Jack

parts.note: to walk out with someone is an old phrase for to court them
Denry Machin is the hero of Arnold Bennett's novel The Card

explanation.surface: A woman chooses between going out with two different men.
explanation.walkthrough: Denry looks like a misprinted name; he is Bennett's cheeky hero, nicknamed 'the Card'.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is one of the face cards, along with the king and queen.

clue.text: Bulk carrier in Eastcheap

parts.note: sounds like a cargo ship, but describes Shakespeare's fat knight, who drinks at the Boar's Head tavern in Eastcheap, London

explanation.walkthrough: A bulk carrier is a cargo ship; here it is a man who carries a great bulk of body.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John, Shakespeare's corpulent knight in the Henry IV plays, haunts a tavern in Eastcheap.

clue.text: Said to be gaga about old hearing device

indicators.note: being gaga means being confused or senile, so the word said is muddled up

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be senile about an old hearing aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be gaga' jumbles SAID into ASDI; the device is wartime submarine-detecting sonar, not a hearing aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Asdic was the early British sonar system for detecting submarines by listening to echoes.

clue.text: Water tank thus used up on bird

indicators.note: on in a down clue places the first piece above the bird
used up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: A water tank has been exhausted by a bird perched on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used up' turns SIC into CIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a tank for storing water, as in a loft or above a lavatory.

clue.text: Help to charm and amuse the court — that's an order

indicators.note: help to, as in taking a helping of a dish, means taking a portion from the words that follow

explanation.surface: An instruction to assist in charming and entertaining the royal court.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across charm, and and amuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandamus is a writ issued by a higher court commanding a lower body to perform a duty.

clue.text: Bent gaoler pocketing a pound in quick time

indicators.note: pocketing means the rearranged word takes in the other piece
bent means crooked or twisted, so the word is rearranged

parts.note: L stands for libra, a pound

explanation.surface: A corrupt prison officer quickly pockets a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' rearranges GAOLER (British for jailer) to ALEGRO, which takes the L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical direction meaning brisk or lively tempo.

clue.text: Something owed to a royal nurse

parts.note: R stands for rex or regina, king or queen
to rear is to nurse or bring up

explanation.surface: A debt is due to a nurse in the royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrear is an amount overdue for payment.

clue.text: Reinstate the young man in the big hat

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's instruction to restore a deleted word
a son is a young male child

explanation.surface: A cowboy in a wide-brimmed hat is allowed back.
explanation.walkthrough: STET, Latin for 'let it stand', is written beside text that was struck out but should stay.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is the wide-brimmed, high-crowned cowboy headgear.

clue.text: Top audience of forty

indicators.note: an audience hears things, so what is wanted is the spoken form

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Forty people make the best audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' is a verb: to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo or surpass others.

clue.text: One who acclaims a result wildly

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters of a result are thrown about

explanation.surface: A fan cheers a result with wild enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who greets or hails another with praise is honouring them.

clue.text: The Head's trophy

parts.note: sounds like a school head teacher's prize, but describes skin and hair taken from an enemy's head as a token of victory

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' suggests a head teacher; here it is the top of a skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin with hair cut from a defeated enemy's crown was kept as a war token.

clue.text: lago having words, using the old tongue

parts.note: in Othello, Iago holds the rank of ancient, an old word for an ensign or standard-bearer
words in the sense of speech or vocabulary is language

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's villain argues, speaking an archaic dialect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having words' suggests a quarrel; Iago is Othello's ancient, his rank in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue of former times, such as Latin or Sanskrit, is a classical speech.

clue.text: Iron rule for a cheater, say

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a line is a ruled stroke, or a rule of conduct

explanation.surface: A strict regulation for dealing with someone who cheats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheater, say' asks us to hear cheetah: the big cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah, which a cheater sounds like, is a member of the cat family.

clue.text: Champion life-guard?

definitions.meaning: to champion a cause is to support and defend it, so a champion is a defender of it
playfully, someone who keeps a swimmer afloat literally keeps them up

explanation.definitionFit: A supporter or defender of a cause, and whimsically one who holds a person above water.
